note: Small boat-ramp access on the Grand River at the south edge of Brunswick, one block south of Highway 24 across the railroad. The primitive camping area is the river side of the large gravel lot, beside a picnic pavilion and privy; a band of bank trees stands between the lot and the river. Spot length is not published. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: MDC 'Individual Campsites' - one mapped Primitive Camping Area at the river edge of the gravel lot (the stored pin), free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit; privy added. Riverview not supported from the camp (wooded bank band; the only opening is the ramp lane) - suggest not waterfront. Phone matches.
flags: WATERFRONT (stored riverview): suggest DOWNGRADE to not waterfront. GIS camping point 474 (= stored pin) sits at the south edge of the gravel lot beside the pavilion. Measured on the 0.22 m/px leaf-off frame it is ~50 m from the Grand River (river ~100 m+ wide), and the ground between is a 35-40 m band of bank trees and brush (dense trunks even leaf-off). MDC's own photo of the lot (media gallery, summer) shows a solid wall of full-leaf trees behind the gravel. The only opening to the water is the concrete ramp lane ~25 m west of the point, which is a ramp corridor, not the camp. No open sightline from the camp; unsure resolves down.

INCLUSION/FIT: area page lists 'Camping: Individual Campsites' ('This area offers access to the Grand River with a boat ramp.'); the 08/09 map shows the Primitive Camping Area symbol at the river edge of the parking lot with a pavilion, privy and accessible symbol. The lot is a ~80 x 60 m gravel lot reached from Polk Street (paved town street) - a 23-ft rig fits. Standard 3CSR 10-11 140 camping text only.
